gaps.note: The reader does not know what the main theorem states. The page says only that it is a statement about the running time cost and that its bound is an O(·) bound in n; it neither explains the theorem nor links to a page for it.

gaps.term: bounds on the way to the main theorem
gaps.quote: so every bound on the way to it is a bound on the running time cost of one specific machine
gaps.note: This follows only from the main theorem being a statement about the running time cost, which the reader cannot see. The page gives no reason why each intermediate bound concerns one fixed machine.

gaps.term: step count in the scanning example
gaps.quote: On the input $0001$ of length $4$ it takes $4$ steps
gaps.note: The page does not give the scanning machine's moves or say how reading a cell, the first cell, or halting is counted. So the reader cannot check that the count is 4 for the input 0001 or for the input 0000.

gaps.quote: and an input that is all zeros is the one that realises it
gaps.note: The page shows only that the all-zero input takes 4 steps. It does not show that no other input of length 4 takes more, and it does not say the alphabet is binary, which the count of 16 inputs needs. The reader cannot check the maximum.
